R001.fact: For an extended nonnegative real x and k∈ℕ, if x≤(k:ℝ≥0∞), then 0≤x≤(k:ℝ≥0∞)<∞, 0≤x.toReal≤(k:ℝ), and ENNReal.ofReal(x.toReal)=x.

grounds.reason: The bound n is a natural number, so its extended nonnegative real embedding is finite.
At x=dimH E and k=n, E008 supplies x≤k.
Hausdorff dimension has codomain ℝ≥0∞.
D is x.toReal; toReal and ofReal have the specified finite-value and embedding meanings.

R001.justification: Zero is the least extended nonnegative real, and the embedding of a natural number has finite value. An element below that finite bound cannot be infinity, hence is the embedding of a unique real u≥0. Order on finite embedded values is ordinary real order, so u≤k. By the finite-value definition toReal x=u; since u≥0, ofReal u embeds u unchanged and thus equals x. This routine order identification applies also when k=0.

R002.fact: For real s,t≥0, ENNReal.ofReal s≤ENNReal.ofReal t iff s≤t, and ENNReal.ofReal s<ENNReal.ofReal t iff s<t. For every real r, ENNReal.ofReal r<∞. For s,t≥0, ENNReal.ofReal(s+t)=ENNReal.ofReal s+ENNReal.ofReal t, and ENNReal.ofReal 1=1.

grounds.reason: ofReal is the canonical embedding of max(r,0) into the extended nonnegative reals.
D is nonnegative and its embedding equals dimH E.
Under L1, q>D≥0; the displayed comparison therefore lies in the nonnegative range.

R002.justification: The extended nonnegative reals adjoin a greatest element to the nonnegative real half-line. On finite nonnegative values, the embedding preserves and reflects the ordinary real order and preserves addition; its image contains only finite values. Applying the truncation r↦max(r,0) proves finiteness for all real r. These facts justify S001, the finite bound in S006, the order reflection in S007 and the final embedding/addition in S008.

R002.fact: If x∈ℝ≥0∞ satisfies x<∞, then x.toReal≥0 and ENNReal.ofReal(x.toReal)=x. Consequently, for real c≥0, x≤ENNReal.ofReal c implies x.toReal≤c.

grounds.reason: F006 proves dimH F<∞ before T is introduced.
toReal returns the real value of a finite extended nonnegative real.
F005 supplies the comparison at every real b>D.
D≥0 ensures b+1≥0 whenever b>D.

R002.justification: A finite extended nonnegative real is represented by a unique nonnegative real; toReal returns this representative and ofReal embeds it back. Substituting that inverse identity into x≤ofReal c and reflecting order on nonnegative representatives proves the last assertion. With x=dimH F and c=b+1, this establishes every clause of F007.

R003.fact: For nonnegative real x,y, the finite embedding e(x)=ENNReal.ofReal x preserves and reflects ≤ and <, has e(0)=0 and e(1)=1, satisfies e(x+y)=e(x)+e(y), and always satisfies e(x)<∞. The extended nonnegative reals are linearly ordered with greatest element ∞; hence ∞≤q implies q=∞, and ¬(a≤b) implies b<a.

grounds.reason: Dimension comparisons and additions take place in the extended nonnegative reals.
ofReal is the stated nonnegative embedding.
D≥0 and dimH E=e(D); local exponent signs are established in S002 and S005 before their comparisons.

R003.justification: The extended nonnegative reals consist of the nonnegative real line with a greatest element adjoined. Finite elements inherit the real order and addition, giving all embedding identities and order reflection. Antisymmetry and linearity give the two order consequences. Thus positivity in S001–S002, the top argument in S004, finite addition in S007 and comparison in S009 use only these routine structural facts.

R003.fact: If q∈ℝ≥0∞ satisfies q<∞, then u=q.toReal is nonnegative and ENNReal.ofReal u=q. For c≥0, q<ENNReal.ofReal c consequently implies u<c.

grounds.reason: F007 gives dimH F<∞ and dimH F<ofReal(D+1).
D>0, so D+1 is nonnegative.
toReal on finite extended nonnegative reals is their real value.

R003.justification: A finite extended nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative real value. Taking toReal recovers that value; embedding it recovers q. Strict comparison then follows from order reflection on the finite nonnegative real part. This establishes exactly the three claims of F008 without assuming finiteness in advance.

R003.fact: V_n×ℝ with distance max(dist(x,x'),dist(t,t')) is a metric space. Equipped with its Borel measurable structure, it satisfies the metric/Borel hypotheses of M002. This Borel structure also agrees with the product of the usual Borel structures on these Euclidean factors.

grounds.reason: The factors are Euclidean metric spaces with Borel structures and the product distance is explicitly max.
F is a subset of this product space.
M002 applies to any subset of a metric space with Borel measurable structure.

R003.justification: The maximum distance satisfies separation, symmetry and the triangle inequality by the corresponding factor properties. Its open balls are products of factor balls, so it induces the product topology. Both Euclidean factors have countable bases, including the singleton case n=0; every open product-space set is a countable union of basic open rectangles. This identifies its Borel sigma algebra with the product Borel sigma algebra. No measurability of F itself is needed.

R004.fact: For x0∈V_n and t,u∈ℝ, dist(x0,x0)=0 and dist(t,u)≥0; hence max(dist(x0,x0),dist(t,u))=dist(t,u).

grounds.reason: V_n is a metric space and the product uses the maximum of factor distances.
ℝ carries its usual metric.
x0 has type V_n and t,u have type ℝ within S002.

R004.justification: The self-distance and nonnegativity statements are metric axioms. Substituting self-distance zero reduces the equality to max(0,d)=d for d≥0, which follows from the definition of maximum. These grounds justify the finite metric calculation already displayed in S002.

R005.fact: For a real u>0, ENNReal.ofReal u>0; also ENNReal.ofReal 0=0. Consequently N001's identity dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D gives positive dimension when D>0, and zero dimension when D=0.

grounds.reason: ofReal is the embedding of max(u,0) into the extended nonnegative reals; D is real.
Provides dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D.
The positive branch explicitly assumes D>0.

R005.justification: For u>0, max(u,0)=u, and the canonical embedding of nonnegative reals into their extension by infinity preserves strict order and zero. At u=0 the truncated value is zero, whose image is zero. Substitution into N001's identity proves the two asserted consequences without additional assumptions.

R006.fact: For x,y∈ℝ≥0∞, if x≤y and y≤x, then x=y; in particular this applies to x=dimH F and y=dimH E+1 without any finiteness assumption.

grounds.reason: Dimensions, comparisons and additions have codomain ℝ≥0∞.
F is precisely the product set appearing in both input statements, with the same max metric.
Supplies x≤y.
Supplies y≤x in the nonempty-E context retained by the output.

R006.justification: The usual extended nonnegative real order restricts to the ordinary antisymmetric order on finite nonnegative real values and has ∞ as its greatest element. If either value is ∞, the opposite inequality forces the other to be ∞; if both are finite, the two real inequalities imply equality. These cases establish precisely the antisymmetry used in S001.

R007.fact: When n=0 and E is a nonempty subset of V_0, E=V_0, and euclideanProduct 0 E is exactly the set of vectors in V_1 whose sole coordinate t lies in [0,1].

grounds.reason: V_0 is the singleton empty-coordinate vector space.
N006 explicitly concerns the given nonempty E; the boundary observation uses exactly this stated condition.
I is exactly [0,1].
F is the product E×I.
With zero initial coordinates, appendCoord 0 has only the final coordinate t.
euclideanProduct 0 E is the image of F under that map.

R007.justification: A nonempty subset of a singleton contains its unique element and hence equals the singleton. Thus every (x,t) in F has the unique empty-coordinate x and t∈I; its appended vector has only coordinate t. Conversely, for every t∈I that unique x belongs to E and supplies a preimage. This proves both image inclusions.

source_steps.text: Apply E008 to the given natural number n and arbitrary subset E of V_n. It gives dimH E≤n and dimH I=1. Dimensions have values in the nonnegative extended reals, so 0≤dimH E. Since the embedded natural number n is finite, dimH E is finite. For a finite nonnegative extended real, toReal is its unique nonnegative real value; consequently D=(dimH E).toReal satisfies 0≤D≤n and ENNReal.ofReal D=dimH E. This is all of the assigned output, also when n=0.

Fix an arbitrary real q and temporarily assume L1: D<q. N001 gives D≥0 and dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D, hence q>0 and dimH E<ENNReal.ofReal q. For nonnegative reals, their embeddings into the extended nonnegative reals preserve strict order.
Apply the first implication of M002 in V_n, with subset E and nonnegative real exponent q. By F001 its strict dimension comparison holds, so μH[q](E)=0.
Apply E003 at the same n,E,q. F001 gives q>0 and F002 is its zero-measure premise. The conclusion is μH[q+1](F)=0, since F is E×I in the max product metric.
Since q>0, the exponent q+1 is nonnegative. Apply the third implication of M002 to F⊆V_n×ℝ at exponent q+1. F003 gives zero measure, hence dimH F≤ENNReal.ofReal(q+1).
Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary q. We have proved the full statement F005: for every real b, D<b implies dimH F≤ENNReal.ofReal(b+1).
Use F005 at b=D+1, for which D<D+1. It yields dimH F≤ENNReal.ofReal(D+2)<∞. The last bound holds because D+2 is an ordinary real number. Thus dimH F is finite.

Define T=(dimH F).toReal. By F006, T≥0 and ENNReal.ofReal T=dimH F. F005 and D≥0 from N001 show that for every real b>D, both T and b+1 are nonnegative and T≤b+1; this follows by comparing their finite nonnegative embeddings.

Temporarily assume L2: T>D+1. Define u=(D+T-1)/2. The inequality D<T-1 gives D<u<T-1 by subtraction and division by 2. F007 applied to u therefore yields T≤u+1<T, a contradiction. Discharge L2 to conclude T≤D+1. By N001, dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D with D≥0; thus ENNReal.ofReal(D+1)=dimH E+1. Embedding T≤D+1 and using F007 proves dimH F≤dimH E+1, which is the assigned output.
To prove the conditional the assigned output, temporarily assume L1: 0<dimH E. N001 gives dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D and D≥0. Order preservation of the nonnegative embedding therefore gives D>0.
Fix an arbitrary real s and temporarily assume L2: 0<s<D. By N001, dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D, so s is positive and ENNReal.ofReal s<dimH E.
Use the second implication of M002 on E⊆V_n with the nonnegative exponent s. The strict comparison from F002 yields μH[s](E)=∞.
Apply E004 at the given n,E and positive real s. It gives μH[s](E)≤μH[s+1](F). The left side is ∞ by F003; since ∞ is the greatest extended nonnegative real, this forces μH[s+1](F)=∞.
Apply the fourth implication of M002 to F in the max product metric at nonnegative exponent s+1. From F004 we obtain ENNReal.ofReal(s+1)≤dimH F.
Discharge L2 and universally quantify s. Under L1 we have F006: for every real b with 0<b<D, ENNReal.ofReal(b+1)≤dimH F.
Still under L1, suppose for contradiction L3: dimH F<dimH E+1. By N001, dimH E+1=ENNReal.ofReal(D+1)<∞, because D≥0 is finite. Hence dimH F<∞.
Define T=(dimH F).toReal. F007 implies T≥0, ENNReal.ofReal T=dimH F, and T<D+1 by order comparison of finite nonnegative embeddings; D+1>0 by F001.

Define v=max(0,T-1) and s0=(v+D)/2. Since D>0 by F001 and T-1<D by F008, we have 0≤v<D. Thus 0<s0<D and T-1≤v<s0. Applying F006 at s0 gives ENNReal.ofReal(s0+1)≤dimH F=ENNReal.ofReal T. Both arguments of ofReal are nonnegative, so s0+1≤T. But T-1<s0 implies T<s0+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3; the linear order now gives dimH E+1≤dimH F under L1.
Discharge L1 by implication introduction. We have proved: if 0<dimH E then dimH E+1≤dimH F. This is the assigned output, and the positive-dimension condition remains precisely its antecedent.
H002 states that E is nonempty. Choose a point x0∈E; the eventual bound on dimH F will not depend on the identity of this witness.

Define f:ℝ→V_n×ℝ by f(t)=(x0,t). For arbitrary reals t,u, the max product metric gives dist(f(t),f(u))=max(dist(x0,x0),dist(t,u))=max(0,dist(t,u))=dist(t,u), because a metric distance is nonnegative. Thus f preserves every pairwise distance and Isometry f holds by D009.
Apply M013 with source ℝ, target V_n×ℝ, map f and subset I. F002 supplies the isometry condition. It yields dimH(f''I)=dimH I.
The image f''I consists exactly of the pairs (x0,t) with t∈I. By F001 the first coordinate is in E. The definition F=E×I therefore gives f''I⊆F.

Use M012 in V_n×ℝ on the inclusion F004 to get dimH(f''I)≤dimH F. By F003 and the interval clause dimH I=1 of N001, its left side equals 1. Thus 1≤dimH F, which is the assigned output. The conclusion contains neither x0 nor f, so the witness introduced from H002 is properly eliminated. The construction also works for V_0.
N001 gives D≥0 and dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D. The real order therefore gives the exhaustive alternatives D>0 or D=0.

In the first branch temporarily assume L1: D>0. N001 implies 0<dimH E by its embedding identity. Apply the implication N003 to obtain dimH E+1≤dimH F. Discharge L1, recording the corresponding conditional bound.

In the other branch temporarily assume L2: D=0. N001 gives dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal 0=0. N004 states 1≤dimH F; since dimH E+1=0+1=1, it is exactly the desired lower bound. Discharge L2 to record this conditional bound.
Eliminate the exhaustive disjunction F001 using F002 and F003. Both branches give the same unconditional inequality dimH E+1≤dimH F. This is the assigned output, including the zero-dimension case.

N002 gives dimH F≤dimH E+1 and N005 gives dimH E+1≤dimH F, in the same extended nonnegative real order and for the same max product metric. Antisymmetry yields dimH F=dimH E+1, exactly the assigned output.

Instantiate E005 at the given n and S=F⊆V_n×ℝ. Its map is the exact append-coordinate map A_n of D007, with max metric on its source and Euclidean metric on its target. It therefore gives dimH(A_n''F)=dimH F. By D008, A_n''F=euclideanProduct n E, so dimH(euclideanProduct n E)=dimH F. This source conclusion is the required change of metric and coordinate identification.

Substitute N006, dimH F=dimH E+1, into F001. Thus dimH(euclideanProduct n E)=dimH E+1 with the required Euclidean metric and coordinate description. The given n and E were arbitrary, so this proves P under the original hypotheses. When n=0, D001 makes V_0 the singleton empty-coordinate vector space, and D007 sends (x,t) to the vector whose sole coordinate is t; hence the same statements cover this boundary case. All measures are those of D003, with the unnormalized diameter-power convention at the positive exponents used in the proof and the dimension convention of D004.

header:
import Mathlib
open scoped ENNReal NNReal MeasureTheory
open Set MeasureTheory
noncomputable section
namespace ProductInterval
abbrev V (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
def interval : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1
def appendCoord (n : ℕ) (p : V n × ℝ) : V (n + 1) :=
  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ).symm
    (Fin.snoc ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ) p.1) p.2)
def euclideanProduct (n : ℕ) (E : Set (V n)) : Set (V (n + 1)) :=
  appendCoord n '' (E ×ˢ interval)
end ProductInterval
namespace ProductInterval
def F (n : ℕ) (E : Set (V n)) : Set (V n × ℝ) := E ×ˢ interval
def D (n : ℕ) (E : Set (V n)) : ℝ := (dimH E).toReal
end ProductInterval

E003.explanation: The exact prepared closed type quantifies over every n, every subset E of Euclidean V n and every real q>0. Its sole additional premise is zero q-measure of E, and its conclusion is zero (q+1)-measure of E ×ˢ [0,1] with the native max product metric. hausdorffMeasure uses the stipulated unnormalized countable diameter-power convention. No compactness, nonemptiness or positive-dimension restriction is added.

E004.explanation: The exact prepared closed type retains arbitrary n and E and the real exponent s>0. It compares the unnormalized s-measure of E to the (s+1)-measure of E ×ˢ [0,1] in ENNReal, with the max product metric. Measure evaluation accepts arbitrary subsets, so no measurability, finiteness or compactness premise is introduced.

E005.explanation: The exact prepared type uses appendCoord n defined by Fin.snoc through EuclideanSpace.equiv: the first n coordinates are x and the last is t. For every subset S of the native max-metric product V n × ℝ it equates the ENNReal Hausdorff dimension of its image in Euclidean V (n+1) to dimH S. These are exactly the specified two metrics and map, including n=0; no extra condition on S appears.

E008.explanation: The prepared conjunction says that every subset E of Euclidean V n has ENNReal dimension at most the natural-number embedding n, and that the real interval [0,1] has dimension one. The finite embedded natural bound implies the source finiteness claim and covers n=0. There is no positivity, compactness or nonemptiness condition.

P.explanation: The public parameters range over all n : ℕ, including zero, and all E : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)). The original roots are exactly IsCompact E and E.Nonempty; no extra hypotheses enter the target. euclideanProduct n E is definitionally the append-coordinate image of E ×ˢ [0,1], hence is exactly the required coordinate subset of Euclidean ℝ^(n+1). The conclusion equates its ENNReal Hausdorff dimension with dimH E+1, using the native dimension whose empty-set value is zero. The max product metric occurs only in intermediate results; T009 specializes E005 to justify the actual metric change. V 0 is the empty-coordinate singleton and appendCoord 0 places t in its sole new coordinate, so the same quantified assertion covers the zero-dimensional ambient case. Compactness remains an original assumption even though the active stronger route does not need it.

conclusion.statement: For every integer n≥0 and every nonempty compact E⊆Euclidean ℝ^n, the coordinate copy of E×[0,1] in Euclidean ℝ^(n+1) has Hausdorff dimension dimH E+1. The coordinate copy consists of (x₁,…,x_n,t) with x∈E and 0≤t≤1; for n=0 it is the unit interval in Euclidean ℝ. Hausdorff measures use the unnormalized diameter-power convention and dimH∅=0.

representation: Use the registry's exact ProductInterval definitions. V n is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), namely PiLp 2 over the finite coordinate type: the parameter 2 specifies the Euclidean norm, while Fin n indexes coordinates. Fin 0 is empty and V 0 is a singleton. The ordinary product V n × ℝ has Mathlib's max metric, as Prod.dist_eq states, and F n E is exactly E ×ˢ interval. The target is the Euclidean coordinate image defined by euclideanProduct, not the max-metric product. E005 supplies its metric transfer, specialized in T009. All sets are arbitrary subsets with their ambient metrics; no measurability condition is imposed on E or covers. Hausdorff measure is MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure at a real exponent; its pinned hausdorffMeasure_apply is precisely the scale supremum of countable diameter-power cover costs, with empty sets costing zero and no normalizing constant. dimH is the ENNReal-valued supremum of embedded nonnegative exponents with infinite measure and uses the ambient Borel structure. Addition by 1 and comparisons of dimensions are in ℝ≥0∞. D n E is only the total real conversion (dimH E).toReal; its nonnegativity, finiteness and inverse identity are proved in T001, not assumed by definition. The native critical-exponent API has exponent d : ℝ≥0: applications in T002/T004 package the positive real exponents as nonnegative reals, whose real coercions are the measure exponents and whose ENNReal coercions equal ofReal of those reals. Native Isometry preserves edist; on the metric spaces used here isometry_iff_dist_eq gives exactly the source distance-preservation predicate. Retain the prepared M002 critical-exponent conjunction and M012/M013 monotonicity and isometry ports as the selected foundation graph requires. Their exact closed types are unchanged; their native content has been inspected. These prepared ports are discharged by the supplied checked foundations, not re-proved as project obligations. Workload/shared-consumer review: T001 is the existing shared N001 export, consumed by both bounds, the interval embedding and the final case split. T002/T004 isolate the independent measure arguments from the finite-real order finishes T003/T005. T006 keeps the nonempty-set witness, its isometric map and image inclusion together; neither escapes. T007/T008 perform only case elimination and antisymmetry. T009 is the explicit metric bridge and T010 substitutes the max-metric result. F and D are the only added shared definitions; there is no new mathematical shared extraction or repeated large auxiliary proof. H001 is retained at the target although the active route needs no compactness.
